explainer.heading: What the poem says
explainer.body: A mother tells her son that her life has not been a “crystal stair” (easy and beautiful). It had tacks, splinters, torn-up boards and bare places with no carpet. Yet she kept climbing, reaching landings, turning corners, sometimes going on in the dark. She tells him not to turn back, sit down on the steps or fall, because she is still climbing.
explainer.example: Theme: perseverance and determination in a hard life.

explainer.heading: Extended metaphor
explainer.body: Life is compared to a staircase throughout. Tacks and splinters = pain and problems; boards torn up and no carpet = poverty and hardship; landings = achievements; turning corners = changes; going in the dark = times without hope or help.

explainer.heading: Tone and language
explainer.body: Tone: loving, honest, encouraging and determined. The mother speaks in informal dialect (“ain’t been no”, “I’se been a-climbin’ on”) which makes her voice real and personal.

explainer.heading: Devices
explainer.body: Repetition: “life for me ain’t been no crystal stair” opens and closes the poem. Anaphora: lines starting with “And” (“And splinters, / And boards torn up, / And places with no carpet…”) and “Don’t you…”. Assonance: repeated vowel sound, e.g. /o/ in “So boy, don’t you turn back”.

explainer.heading: The poet
explainer.body: Langston Hughes was an American poet, novelist and playwright of the Harlem Renaissance (1920–1930), known for his engagement with jazz. Works include “The Weary Blues”, “The Ways of White Folks” and “The Big Sea”.

questions.q: Who is speaking in the poem?
questions.why: A mother speaking to her son.

questions.q: “Life for me ain’t been no crystal stair” means…
options: Her life has not been easy or comfortable
questions.ans: Her life has not been easy or comfortable

questions.q: What do the tacks and splinters represent?
What advice does the mother give her son?
options: Give up when it is hard
Don’t turn back, don’t sit down, don’t fall — keep going
questions.ans: Don’t turn back, don’t sit down, don’t fall — keep going

questions.q: The whole poem compares life to…
Lines beginning with “And splinters, / And boards torn up” show…
questions.why: Repetition at the start of lines.

questions.q: What is the overall tone of the poem?
What does the mother mean by “life for me ain’t been no crystal stair”?
questions.model: She means her life has not been easy, smooth or comfortable like a beautiful crystal staircase; it has been full of hardships.
points: Full of hardships (vs a beautiful crystal stair)

questions.q: How does the poet use the image of a staircase to show the mother’s struggle and determination?
questions.model: The poet compares life to a staircase. The mother’s stair had tacks and splinters (pain), torn-up boards and bare places without carpet (poverty and hardship) — unlike a crystal stair. Still, she kept climbing, reaching landings (achievements), turning corners (changes) and going on even in the dark (times without hope). She urges her son not to turn back or sit down because she is still climbing. The image shows that she never gave up and wants her son to persevere.
points: Staircase = life; crystal stair = easy life
Tacks, splinters, torn boards, no carpet = hardships
Climbing, landings, corners, dark = perseverance through difficulties
Advice to son; message of determination
